newsitem.title: UK: Mark/yen at one-year low as mark sags across board.
newsitem.headline: Mark/yen at one-year low as mark sags across board.

text.p: The mark sank to its lowest level against the yen in nearly a year in Europe on Wednesday, pushed down by the mark's softness across the board and the yen's continued strength against the dollar.

Mark/yen has been weakening since early May in tandem with dollar/yen's weakness. It hit 69.63 yen in morning trade, its lowest since May 24 last year, and was down from 69.97/00 in late European on Tuesday.
Fresh factors emerged this morning to weigh on the beleaguered German currency, pushing mark/yen ever lower.
The mark was dampened against the dollar by a comment by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke, who said a dollar/mark rate of about 1.70 was supported by economic fundamentals.

Dollar/mark built on early European gains as the market took heart from Welteke's comment. The dollar was at 1.7050/55 marks at 1003 GMT, off its session high of 1.7063 but up from 1.6964/69 in late Europe on Tuesday.

Another remark from Welteke knocked the mark down against its European counterparts. He said the 3.0 percent budget deficit-to-GDP criteria for participation in Europe's monetary union was not set in stone.
Welteke added that sustained low budget deficits were more important.
His comment helped drive the mark down on its European crosses with some taking it as an indication of some relaxation of Germany's stance on a strict interpretation of the EMU criteria.
Analysts, however, were sceptical of such an interpretation, saying that the emphasis of Welteke's comment was on the importance of keeping deficits low.
Meanwhile, yen strength against the dollar added to the pressure on mark/yen.

Dollar/yen's swift slide from late last week has come to a halt, but the U.S. currency was still struggling against a solid ceiling at 119 yen. Dollar/yen's recent slide was due to a barrage of verbal intervention from Japanese authorities and expectations of higher Japanese interest rates.
Dollar/yen was at 118.49/59 against 118.65/75 on Tuesday.
